summary: A genuinely mutual NDA on English law that largely tracks the playbook; the points to check are the omission of insurers from Representatives, the missing fraud carve-out in the reliance disclaimer, and an immediate breach-notification duty the playbook does not cover.

findings.quote: each Party, acting as the Receiving Party, hereby covenants, undertakes and agrees with the other Party, acting as the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Obligations bind each Party as Receiving Party in favour of the other, and the Disclosing/Receiving Party definitions work for either side.

findings.quote: whether disclosed before, on or after the Effective Date, in connection with the Purpose
findings.why: The definition covers all information disclosed in connection with the Purpose without a marking requirement and, in (d), includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: use the Confidential Information exclusively for the furtherance of the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, a potential commercial transaction and collaboration between the parties.

findings.quote: can conclusively demonstrate by contemporaneous written records, documentary evidence or other competent proof
findings.why: All four carve-outs appear in 3.1.1 to 3.1.4 and the evidence standard allows written records or other competent proof, though the wording is somewhat heavier than the template.

findings.quote: no Confidential Information is disclosed to any person other than those Representatives and Affiliates who have a demonstrable, strict operational need to know
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted to Representatives and Affiliates (Group) on a need-to-know basis, and 2.1.5 makes the Receiving Party liable for them.

findings.quote: directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, financial auditors, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party or of any Affiliate of that Party
findings.why: The list of permitted Representatives covers advisers and auditors but does not mention insurers, which the playbook position expects.
findings.draft_redline: "Representatives" means, in relation to a Party, the directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, financial auditors, insurers, technical consultants, accountants and professional agents of that Party or of any Affiliate of that Party.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would be grateful if insurers could be added to the list of Representatives, as we may need to share information with our insurers on a confidential basis.

findings.quote: are bound by written confidentiality obligations or professional duties of secrecy that are no less restrictive than the terms and conditions contained herein
findings.why: Written undertakings are required only where the recipient is not already under professional duties of secrecy.
findings.fallback_cited: Requirement for written confidentiality undertakings from advisers who are not under professional duties.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall, subject to applicable legal restrictions:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted and the notice and cooperation duties in 4.1.1 to 4.1.2 are qualified by applicable legal restrictions, with 4.2 giving notice as soon as legally permissible.
findings.fallback_cited: Notice 'where lawful' and cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: exercise all reasonable commercial efforts to obtain a binding written assurance from the presiding court, tribunal or regulatory agency that confidential treatment will be accorded
findings.why: This is a reasonable-efforts duty to obtain confidential treatment rather than a duty to resist disclosure, although the contract is silent on who bears the cost.
findings.fallback_cited: Obligation to use reasonable endeavours to obtain confidential treatment, at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such request or upon such termination or expiration
findings.why: Return or destruction is required within 10 Business Days of written request.

findings.quote: a duly authorised officer of the Receiving Party shall provide the Disclosing Party with a written certification
findings.why: An officer must certify compliance in writing, as the playbook prefers.

findings.quote: electronic backup copies of Confidential Information generated automatically through routine data archiving, disaster recovery and electronic backup systems
findings.why: Automated backups may be retained and 5.4 keeps retained copies confidential.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting, conferring, assigning or transferring
findings.why: All rights and IP stay with the Disclosing Party and no licence or assignment is granted.

findings.quote: without any representation, warranty or guarantee of any kind, whether express, implied, statutory or otherwise
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty, mutually for both Disclosing Parties.

findings.quote: shall be entirely at the Receiving Party's sole risk and discretion
findings.why: The reliance disclaimer excludes the Disclosing Party's exposure for reliance with no carve-out for fraud, which the playbook position requires.
findings.draft_redline: The Receiving Party acknowledges and agrees that any reliance upon, utilisation of, or commercial application of any Confidential Information shall be entirely at the Receiving Party's sole risk and discretion, save that nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes liability for fraud.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to add a short carve-out so that the reliance disclaimer does not limit liability for fraud, which applies equally to both parties.

findings.quote: Neither this Agreement, nor the disclosure or receipt of any Confidential Information, shall constitute, create, imply or evidence an obligation by either Party to enter into any further commercial agreement
findings.why: Neither party is obliged to proceed to a further transaction, as the playbook prefers.

findings.quote: is not intended to involve the transfer, sharing or processing of any personal data
findings.why: Personal data is limited to business contact details, with a separate data processing or sharing agreement required under 7.3 before anything more is shared.

findings.quote: continue in full force and effect for a fixed period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: A three-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early is within the 1 to 3 year range.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years from the effective date of such expiration or termination
findings.why: Survival of five years is at the top of the 2 to 5 year acceptable range.

findings.quote: shall continue in full force and effect without limitation in time for so long as such information retains its legal status as a Trade Secret
findings.why: Indefinite protection is limited to Trade Secrets while they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: shall be entitled, without the necessity of posting any bond or other security, and without proving actual damages, to seek and obtain immediate injunctive relief
findings.why: Injunctive relief is available to either party as Disclosing Party and is cumulative under 9.3; the wording is strong but mutual.
findings.fallback_cited: Strongly worded but mutual equitable relief.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer, novate, charge, encumber, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner
findings.why: Neither party may assign without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, decrypt or otherwise attempt to derive the source code
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: shall be governed by, construed, interpreted and enforced in accordance with the substantive laws of England and Wales
findings.why: The governing law is England and Wales.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.

findings.quote: shall immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon becoming aware of any actual, suspected or threatened unauthorised access
findings.why: This breach-notification and cooperation duty, triggered even by suspected or threatened incidents and requiring immediate notice, is not covered by any playbook rule.
findings.draft_redline: The Receiving Party shall promptly notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon becoming aware of any actual unauthorised access to, or use or disclosure of, the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, and shall provide reasonable cooperation to investigate and remedy it.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are happy to include a mutual breach-notification obligation, but would prefer it to require prompt notice of actual incidents with reasonable cooperation.
